title: Python: a class-body read of a name the class body binds is never resolved through an enclosing function's binding, Rule 6d's single-binding shortcut included (DEC-303 (a73))
description: HOLD, wrong edge on dev. Filed record-only under DEC-303 (a73) (N3 of (a72) item 3; relayed by the leader 2026-11-26). Found by GCLI-112's round 3 review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#220 (landed 3a422ec1). RULE (a73) item 2: a class-body read of a name the class body binds ANYWHERE is never resolved through an enclosing function's binding. That includes Rule 6d's single-binding shortcut (knownClassOf, calls.ts), which takes the same guard #220 gave the multi-binding path (enumerableBindings, via withoutTypeParameterScopes). It should only REMOVE edges. Any CREATED in-repo edge on the five pins comes to opum-doc before the PR; removed edges are reported with the PR. Schedule per (a73) item 3: right after GCLI-112, before the (a25) attribute-write rule (GCLI-140) and ahead of the rest of GCLI-140 to 143; two review rounds under DEC-161's cap; the (a36) item 8 pre-registration (GCLI-143) waits for it. MEASURED on origin/dev (before #220; identical on #220's head): source = class C with def run; def outer(): x = C() [one binding, or x = C(); x = C() for two]; class Outer: <READ> then from m import X as x (m.X has run). Forms: eager y = x.run(); lazy alias type A = x.run(); lazy generic alias type A[T] = x.run(). One binding: all three give inRepo 1 with an edge to C.run (WRONG). Two bindings: all three REFUSED (inRepo 0, receiver 1, no edge), because Rule 6d returns null and R4 reaches the enumerableBindings class-body guard. RUNTIME EVIDENCE (CPython, python3 -I): def outer(): x = C(); class Outer: try: y = x.run() except Exception as e: y = type(e).__name__ + ': ' + str(e); x = 1; return Outer.y gives 'NameError: name x is not defined': a class body reads a name it binds from the class, then globals, then builtins, never from the enclosing function; the two lazy aliases evaluate after the body has bound x to the import. glyph-cli picks the build. Not started; the leader briefs it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The three forms (eager read, type A, type A[T]) with ONE binding of x in the enclosing function assert toEqual(REFUSED) and no C.run edge: red on origin/dev, green after, each measured by running both
The two-binding twins stay REFUSED (they are refused today); a single-binding twin with no class-body binding of x keeps resolving through the enclosing function
A mutant that drops the guard turns the one-binding fixtures red
The five-pin delta: any CREATED in-repo edge comes to opum-doc before the PR; removed edges are listed with the PR; two review rounds at most (DEC-161)

implementationNotes: GCLI-144 built per DEC-303 (a73): lookupBindings (src/python/calls.ts) now sets skipFunctions when the starting class body holds the name but every binding of it is filtered out by Rule 38 (an import after the read); the walk then skips function and lambda scopes and reaches the module scope, then the builtins, which is LOAD_NAME. One central change, so Rule 6d's single-binding shortcut and every other rule that reads through lookupBindings take it, with enumerableBindings' own guard (GCLI-112) unchanged. Fixtures (describe GCLI-144, 11): the three one-binding forms (eager read, type A, type A[T]) assert toEqual(REFUSED) and no C.run, red on origin/dev 4e186bfb (3 fail, 8 pass) and green at the head; the two-binding twins stay REFUSED and pass on both; a no-class-binding twin keeps resolving through the enclosing function; a binding BEFORE the read is the class's own; a module-level binding is still read. Mutant (the guard dropped) turns exactly the three one-binding fixtures red. Five-pin cmp IDENTICAL to origin/dev, so no created and no removed edge; bun test 1185 pass.

REBUILT removal-only (leader's decision after the central build was found to CREATE or REPLACE edges: module x = D() gave D.run, an outer def len gave the builtin, a module def replaced an outer def): lookupBindings no longer skips function scopes; when the starting class body's Rule 38 filter emptied the name's bindings and the result is found in an enclosing FUNCTION scope it returns classBodyShadowed, and the consumers that can yield an edge turn that into unresolved or null only: resolveBareName (unresolved rebound), knownClassOf (Rule 6d), isExternalImportReceiver (false), the callable-instance lookup (null), hasReplacingDecorator (true, refuse). A result found at module scope is unflagged (globals read the same binding; unchanged). The other 8 lookupBindings sites cannot yield an edge from a flagged result (no use position so the flag cannot arise, or a boolean 'found anything', or enumerableBindings which already returns null whenever the class binds the name). Proof: the 3 one-binding forms REFUSED, red on dev; two-binding twins still REFUSED; constructed cases a-k assert the removal-only outcome (a refused not D.run, b refused, c unchanged, d, e, f nameNotBound not the builtin or module def, g unchanged, h no __call__ edge, i not external, k no method edge); 20 fixtures, 10 red on dev. Mutants: each consumer family dropped goes red (resolveBareName 3, knownClassOf 5, isExternalImportReceiver 1, callable 1, hasReplacingDecorator 1), flag never set 9, module exception dropped 1. Differential dev vs head over 126 constructed sources: 0 cases with a created edge, 11 with a removed edge, 0 bin gains. Five-pin cmp IDENTICAL; bun test 1194 pass.

OPTION B added (leader, opum-doc's runtime basis): a lazy alias value in a class body (type A = ..., type A[T] = ..., generic or not) is evaluated after the class body ran, so it sees the class's FINAL bindings, never an earlier or enclosing one. The walker now reads such a value in a type-parameter scope marked Scope.lazyAlias (an empty one for a non-generic alias), and lookupBindings returns the class's binding flagged classBodyShadowed whenever the class body binds the name ANYWHERE; the same consumers refuse it, so it only removes edges. The eager module-level read is unchanged. Measured (module x = C(), no function): eager resolves C.run as on dev; type A and type A[T] give C.run on dev and are REFUSED on the head. Fixtures: 27 in describe GCLI-144 (14 fail on dev). Mutants red: mark not set 4, class check dropped 4, non-generic wrapper dropped 2, flag not tracked 4. Differential dev vs head over 378 constructed sources (adds lazy aliases with module binding, enclosing function binding, class binding before or after or none, lambda, comprehension, call, external, nested class): 0 created edges, 131 removed, 0 bin gains. Five-pin cmp IDENTICAL; bun test 1201 pass.

Round 1 (Opus, head 7ace2acb) BLOCK, one head-only edge, confirmed by running: a NON-generic class-body alias had no scope of its own on dev, so a comprehension target or walrus in its value was recorded on the class body; option B's lazy marker scope took those bindings off the class, so (1) module x = C(), type A = [x for x in ()], y = x.run() gave C.run (dev: receiver), (2) the same with x = C() in def outer(), (3) self.helper() resolved Outer.helper when the alias bound helper (dev refused), plus the walrus variants. Fix: the empty lazy scope of a non-generic alias carries bindsInto (the class), and addBinding records on it, so dev's bindings are unchanged. Fixtures: 4 (comprehension and walrus for cases 1, 2, 3, plus an unrelated-name twin): red on 7ace2acb (3 fail), green on dev and the head; mutant (bindsInto ignored) red (3). Differential widened to 450 sources (adds comprehension, walrus, nested comprehension and lambda aliases, generic or not, with reads before and after and method calls through the bound name): head 0 head-only edges, 131 removed, 0 bin gains; 7ace2acb on the same corpus had 26 head-only edges (positive control). Five-pin cmp IDENTICAL; bun test 1205.
